root_cause.text: `inet6_addr_del()` in `net/ipv6/addrconf.c` dereferenced the removed `inet6_ifaddr`’s `ifp->flags` after `ipv6_del_addr(ifp)` had already freed it for managed temporary addresses, causing a use-after-free.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `ipv6_del_addr(ifp)` below the check `if (!(ifp->flags & IFA_F_TEMPORARY) && (ifp->flags & IFA_F_MANAGETEMPADDR)) delete_tempaddrs(idev, ifp);`, and the commit message explicitly says the bug was “accidentally moved `ipv6_del_addr()` for `mngtmpaddr` before reading its `ifp->flags` for temporary addresses in `inet6_addr_del()`.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Reorder IPv6 address deletion so managed temporary addresses are cleaned up before the target address is freed.
intent_record.what: In inet6_addr_del(), the call to ipv6_del_addr(ifp) was moved down: it now occurs after the conditional delete_tempaddrs(idev, ifp) block instead of before it.
intent_record.how: When deleting an IPv6 address, any managed temporary addresses are now removed first, while the address being deleted is freed afterward. This changes the ordering so temporary-address cleanup can still inspect and act on the address state before it is removed.

grouping_result.intent: Reorder IPv6 address deletion so managed temporary addresses are cleaned up before the target address is freed.

candidates.rationale: This frees the target inet6_ifaddr before the subsequent check of ifp->flags, so later dereference of ifp->flags can become a use-after-free for managed temporary addresses.

This continuation also reads ifp->flags after the address object may already have been freed, contributing to the invalid post-free access.
